target_surface: BHP Warehouse Packing Tracker account-separated operational worklists
problem: The two fixed Bol sources are technically qualified but currently rendered as one combined scanner worklist.

nodes.label: source-qualified scan verification
nodes.evidence: index.html processScan and server application routes

nodes.label: source-qualified accepted/cancelled and source-unqualified STOP history
nodes.evidence: server/application.mjs statePayload and ScannerRepository workday/tracking identity

nodes.label: fixture tests and released desktop/mobile station review

edges.evidence: A visible tab is the explicit requested separation.
Configured fixed accounts decide whether a second tab exists.
The active account determines every source-qualified row and metric.
A cross-source matching code remains a global fail-closed snapshot condition because package persistence is keyed by workday and tracking code.
A scan must use the shipment and account from the active view.
Live outcomes determine source-qualified progress or shared safety review.
Desktop/mobile must prove tab selection, focus, and scoped content.

order_1: make account context explicit before the scan action
order_2: scope worklist and tracking lookup to the selected source
prevent tab changes during active verification
order_3: render accepted/cancelled per source while retaining unassigned STOP safety history
feedback_loops: An unknown code triggers complete snapshot refresh; if verification is still incomplete, the decision remains STOP and scanning stays fail closed.

verification_edges.verification: fixture browser assertions show exclusive primary/client rows and counts after the complete snapshot validates
scan request captures the selected fixed account and rejects wrong-source lookups
same-code cross-source collision remains blocked before scanning; source-qualified state remains scoped and source-unqualified STOP state remains visible
current released desktop/mobile visual receipt shows selected tab and no overflow

local_isolation_proof: No source-qualified renderer may read the combined snapshot directly; it must use the active-source selector helper, while the only combined tracking index remains a fail-closed collision validator.
decision: Use one selected-source presentation layer over the already complete atomic snapshot, retaining the existing cross-source collision block rather than broadening into a persistence-key migration.
